title: Temporal Fade A/B Scheduler — staged time-windowed traffic phasing and rollback rehearsal
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Design a Console UI for scheduling staged A/B traffic shifts that fade traffic between variants over configurable time windows, with preflight simulation and a rollback rehearsal mode. The flow should allow product and platform teams to author time-based traffic curves, preview estimated cost and latency impact, rehearse an emergency rollback, and export a deterministic schedule for the serving runtime.
context: Current rollouts UI supports discrete percent steps and immediate traffic swaps. Customers have asked for time-windowed phasing (e.g., 0->40% over 15 minutes, then 40->80% overnight) and a way to rehearse rollback sequences without touching live traffic. This design explores a temporal "fade" metaphor with a timeline editor, simulation preview, and a 'rehearsal' sandbox that runs the same signals against recorded telemetry.
goals: Enable authors to define traffic transitions as continuous fades over a time window
Provide a safe rehearsal mode that simulates rollback paths against historical signals
Surface cost and latency deltas for each schedule segment
Keep the schedule authoring UX accessible to non-designers (PMs, SREs) while supporting advanced controls for platform teams
user_stories: As a product manager, I want to schedule a 30-minute gradual ramp from control to variant so I can monitor stability during the ramp
As an SRE, I want to run a rollback rehearsal in a sandbox so I can validate rollback steps without affecting production
As a billing owner, I want to see estimated token and GPU cost implications for each phased segment before rollout
As an engineer, I need the schedule export to map to the runtime's rollout schema (v2) so the backend can apply it exactly
acceptance_criteria: Timeline editor prototype allows creating at least three sequential fade segments with start/end times and easing curve selection
Simulation panel shows estimated latency, token count, and cost delta per segment based on representative traffic profile
Rollback rehearsal can be initiated from the UI and produces a deterministic step list identical to the live schedule export
Design tokens and accessibility contrast pass internal a11y checklist and keyboard-only interactions are supported
Final Figma spec includes component states for editing, hover previews, emergency stop, and confirmation flows
design_notes: Primary pattern: horizontal timeline with layered lanes: variants, audience selectors, metrics overlays
Edit handle: dual-handle curve controls that support linear, ease-in/out, and custom bezier — display numeric percent at keyframes
Preview scrubber: live simulation scrubber that animates traffic % and updates metric sparklines
Rehearsal mode: lightweight sandbox toggle that runs the rollout algorithm against archived telemetry (read-only) and shows a step-by-step replay
Failure affordance: prominent 'Emergency Pause' with rollback quick actions (return to last stable snapshot or shift traffic to fallback variant)
Cost overlay: show per-segment delta with expected unit (tokens, GPU-minutes) and a short help tooltip linking to Redwood Optimize docs
Export format: JSON schedule that includes segments, easing, audience filters, and metadata for audit logging
Telemetry hooks: each schedule change should emit diffable events so Console can show a change log and link to audit traces
review_feedback: PM (Diego Alvarez): 'Love the rehearsal idea. Need a compact view for quick checks when oncall is paging.'
Engineering (Sofia Martinez): 'Runtime needs an explicit 'preserve-kv-cache' flag in schedule export; can add in ENG-23210 — blocking for handoff.'
Security (Aisha Rahman): 'Audit log field must include actor, IP, and schedule-hash. Add retention note in PRD.'
Design Review (Marcus Lee): 'Microinteraction for handle snapping feels slow — tighten easing and increase hit target to 12px.'
Accessibility (Ruth Kim): 'Timeline contrast borderline; propose darker stroke and high-contrast mode toggle.'
decisions: Adopt timeline-as-canvas pattern rather than stepper UI to better express continuous fades
Include both percentage and absolute exposure preview (percent + estimated QPS) in simulation panel
Store schedules as 'rollout-schedule-v2' JSON; runtime and console teams will align on keys (ENG-23145)
Expose a readonly 'rehearsal-report' artifact that can be saved to the project's artifacts for audits
open_issues: Finalize naming for easing curves (linear, accelerate, decelerate, custom) across Console and Runtime
Decide retention period for rehearsal artifacts (security asks 90 days, product prefers 30)
next_steps: Iterate Figma prototype based on feedback and produce 4:3 walkthrough video for PM review
Handoff session with ENG (eng sync 2025-03-04) to map schedule JSON to runtime API and validate performance impacts
Accessibility pass and a11y QA ticket creation
Add small-scope MVP to roadmap: create, simulate, export; postpone recurrence scheduling to next cycle
